history_summary.value: The Thuringian comes from the Thuringia region of Germany, where it was first recorded in 1793 and known as the Thuringer Pausbackchen before it was standardised as the Thuringer Barthuhn in 1907. Bred as a dual-purpose farm bird, it is now kept mainly for shows and has been exhibited in Britain since about 2000.

sources.publisher: The Poultry Club of Great Britain

summary.value: The Thuringian is a rare bearded chicken from the Thuringian Forest area of central Germany. Records of it go back to 1793, and it was standardised under the German name Thuringer Barthuhn in 1907. It was meant as a dual purpose farm bird, but today it is mostly seen at poultry shows, and British exhibitors have shown it since about 2000, first in chamois and silver spangled colors. A full beard and muffs give it a round, chubby cheeked face, and the comb is very small, which helps in cold weather. Hens lay about 160 eggs a year. They seldom go broody, but a sitting hen guards her chicks fiercely. The birds are friendly and tame and like to explore, so they do best with room to free range and can make good pets.
